records.query: Need the patient's family history and any genetic testing results to definitively exclude inherited deep stromal corneal dystrophy, as well as histopathological examination if available to confirm the degenerative nature of the posterior corneal rings; these are critical for solidifying the age-related posterior crocodile shagreen diagnosis.

bindings.label: Bilateral symmetric concentric ring-shaped opacities in posterior corneal stroma

Patient is a man in his 70s, presented for routine ophthalmic examination with no specific ocular symptoms, no history of eye surgery; annual physical exam showed no abnormalities with lipid and glucose levels within normal range.

Right eye examination: best spectacle-corrected visual acuity 20/20, normal conjunctiva and adnexa, cornea with normal luster and even surface, no distinct arcus senilis, normal anterior stroma; 4 symmetric complete concentric ring-shaped opacities in posterior corneal stroma, outermost ring ~4mm from limbus, vertical diameters 6.0mm, 4.8mm, 4.5mm, 3.6mm; ring surfaces smooth without deposits, pigmentation, or serrations; peripheral cornea with posterior crocodile shagreen; corneal sensations normal.
Left eye examination: similar findings plus small nasal pterygium; keratometry readings 43.4×43.4 D OD and 43.0×44.8 D OS; mild nuclear sclerosis of crystalline lens in both eyes.
Age-related posterior corneal degeneration (e.g., posterior crocodile shagreen)
In vivo confocal microscopy shows long bandlike structures with thin streaks and no cellular infiltration, consistent with posterior crocodile shagreen
